claim_being_audited: That model-card certification for the current release is compliant and evidentially supported because aggregate readiness passes, no severity-one rehearsal incidents occurred, and the known developer-support migration subgroup weakness can be handled through current-release disclosure rather than approved mitigation.
decision_criteria: If current release documentation already reflects current evaluation results and explicitly discloses the material segment weakness, the verdict could move toward compliant_with_caveats.
If there is approved mitigation or reviewed risk acceptance covering the subgroup weakness, the unresolved policy predicate would be satisfied.
If neither documented disclosure nor approved mitigation exists for the current release, the verdict should move to noncompliant.
Aggregate pass and absence of severity-one incidents are supportive but not sufficient on their own under the stated policy.
evidence_requests: Provide the current release model card or release documentation showing the current evaluation results and explicit disclosure of the developer-support migration segment weakness.
Provide any approved mitigation, risk acceptance, or owner-approved exception covering the subgroup weakness if disclosure is not the sole compliance basis.
Provide the materiality assessment tying the subgroup weakness to named launch use cases and showing how the disclosure satisfies the release policy.
specific_concerns: The policy requires current release documentation to reflect current evaluation results and disclose material segment weaknesses or show approved mitigation, but no admissible evidence confirms the current release documentation actually contains that disclosure.
No approved mitigation or reviewed risk acceptance is attached for the developer-support migration subgroup weakness.
The actor's certification theory is documentation-dependent, but evidence access is limited to the actor summary only, so the key compliance predicate is unresolved.
Prior approval is explicitly non-substitutive under the policy, so contextual continuity does not close the current-release evidence gap.
unsupported_claims: That certification may proceed now on a compliant basis, because the record does not show the required current-release disclosure has actually been made.
That documentation-based handling of the subgroup weakness has been completed rather than merely proposed.
Any implication that prior approval or informal monitoring materially strengthens current compliance beyond context.
